worked: Single, age 63. Taxable Social Security comes out of the income test (Lines 1-3): the measure is exactly 25,000, so the 6,000 is whole. Federal taxable Social Security: other income 25,000.00 + half of benefits 10,000.00 = provisional 35,000.00; 85% x (35,000.00 - 34,000.00) + 4,500.00 = 5,350.00. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 19,000.00 + pensions 6,000.00 + taxable Social Security 5,350.00 = 30,350.00. Federal taxable income = 30,350.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 14,600.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 30,350.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 30,350.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 30,350.00 - 0.00 = 30,350.00. MO-A Part 3 Section C (Y, age 63): Line 1 5,350.00; Line 3 5,350.00 (62 or older by December 31). Section C Line 4 total 5,350.00. Section B: Line 1 30,350.00; Line 2 5,350.00; Line 3 25,000.00; Line 4 25,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 6Y 6,000.00, Line 7Y 6,000.00; Line 8 6,000.00; Line 9 6,000.00. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 11,350.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 26 subtotal 30,350.00 - 11,350.00 - 15,750.00 = 3,250.00. Line 29 taxable income 3,250.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 1,313.00 = 26.26 + 2.5% x 624.00 = 15.6; total 41.86 = 41.86. The chart and Tax Calculation Worksheet (instructions p21) round to the dollar and give 42; expected keeps the bands. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 30,350.00 - Line 8 11,350.00 = 19,000.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 30,350.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.
The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).
